source.title: 静夜思
source.author: 李白
source.text:
床前明月光，疑是地上霜。
举头望明月，低头思故乡。

translation:
Before my bed the bright moonlight falls,
I take it for frost upon the ground.
I raise my head and gaze at the bright moon;
I lower it, and think of home.

source.title: 鹿柴
source.author: 王维
source.text:
空山不见人，但闻人语响。
返景入深林，复照青苔上。

translation:
Deer Enclosure

Empty mountain, no one in sight—
only voices echo.
Returning light enters the deep wood
and falls again upon the green moss.

source.title: 送元二使安西
source.author: 王维
source.text:
渭城朝雨浥轻尘，客舍青青柳色新。
劝君更尽一杯酒，西出阳关无故人。

translation:
Morning rain at Weicheng dampens the fine dust;
The guest house green, the willows newly bright.
Drink yet one more cup of wine, I urge you—
West of Yang Pass, no old friends remain.

source.title: 黄鹤楼送孟浩然之广陵
source.author: 李白
source.text:
故人西辞黄鹤楼，烟花三月下扬州。
孤帆远影碧空尽，唯见长江天际流。

translation:
My old friend takes leave of Yellow Crane Tower in the west,
In mist and blossoms of March, he sails down to Yangzhou.
A lone sail's far shadow fades into the blue—
I see only the Yangtze flowing to the edge of the sky.

source.title: 春望
source.author: 杜甫
source.text:
国破山河在，城春草木深。
感时花溅泪，恨别鸟惊心。
烽火连三月，家书抵万金。
白头搔更短，浑欲不胜簪。

translation:
The realm lies broken; hills and rivers remain,
The city in spring, grass and trees grow deep.
Moved by the times, flowers splash with tears;
Bitter at parting, birds startle the heart.
Beacon fires have burned three months on end;
A letter from home is worth ten thousand in gold.
I scratch my white hair — it grows yet shorter,
So short it will scarcely hold a hairpin.

source.title: 琵琶行
source.author: 白居易
source.text:
浔阳江头夜送客，枫叶荻花秋瑟瑟。
主人下马客在船，举酒欲饮无管弦。
醉不成欢惨将别，别时茫茫江浸月。
忽闻水上琵琶声，主人忘归客不发。
寻声暗问弹者谁，琵琶声停欲语迟。
移船相近邀相见，添酒回灯重开宴。
千呼万唤始出来，犹抱琵琶半遮面。
转轴拨弦三两声，未成曲调先有情。
弦弦掩抑声声思，似诉平生不得志。
低眉信手续续弹，说尽心中无限事。
轻拢慢捻抹复挑，初为霓裳后六幺。
大弦嘈嘈如急雨，小弦切切如私语。
嘈嘈切切错杂弹，大珠小珠落玉盘。
间关莺语花底滑，幽咽泉流冰下难。
冰泉冷涩弦凝绝，凝绝不通声暂歇。
别有幽愁暗恨生，此时无声胜有声。
银瓶乍破水浆迸，铁骑突出刀枪鸣。
曲终收拨当心画，四弦一声如裂帛。
东船西舫悄无言，唯见江心秋月白。
沉吟放拨插弦中，整顿衣裳起敛容。
自言本是京城女，家在虾蟆陵下住。
十三学得琵琶成，名属教坊第一部。
曲罢曾教善才服，妆成每被秋娘妒。
五陵年少争缠头，一曲红绡不知数。
钿头银篦击节碎，血色罗裙翻酒污。
今年欢笑复明年，秋月春风等闲度。
弟走从军阿姨死，暮去朝来颜色故。
门前冷落鞍马稀，老大嫁作商人妇。
商人重利轻别离，前月浮梁买茶去。
去来江口守空船，绕船月明江水寒。
夜深忽梦少年事，梦啼妆泪红阑干。
我闻琵琶已叹息，又闻此语重唧唧。
同是天涯沦落人，相逢何必曾相识！
我从去年辞帝京，谪居卧病浔阳城。
浔阳地僻无音乐，终岁不闻丝竹声。
住近湓江地低湿，黄芦苦竹绕宅生。
其间旦暮闻何物？杜鹃啼血猿哀鸣。
春江花朝秋月夜，往往取酒还独倾。
岂无山歌与村笛？呕哑嘲哳难为听。
今夜闻君琵琶语，如听仙乐耳暂明。
莫辞更坐弹一曲，为君翻作琵琶行。
感我此言良久立，却坐促弦弦转急。
凄凄不似向前声，满座重闻皆掩泣。
座中泣下谁最多？江州司马青衫湿。

translation:
Song of the Pipa
by Bai Juyi

That night by the Xunyang riverbank I saw a guest off;
maple leaves and reed flowers rustling in the autumn.
The host dismounted, the guest sat in the boat;
we raised our cups to drink, but there was no music.
Drunk, yet without joy, we faced the bleak parting;
at parting the boundless river lay steeped in moonlight.

Then a pipa sounded on the water —
the host forgot to return, the guest did not set off.
Following the sound, I asked softly who was playing;
the pipa stopped, and she hesitated to speak.
We moved our boat near and asked her to show herself;
more wine, the lamps relit, the feast spread again.
Only after a thousand calls did she come out,
still holding the pipa, half-veiling her face.

She turned the pegs, plucked two or three notes —
before a melody had formed, the feeling was there.
Every string restrained, every note heavy with thought,
as if telling a life whose aims were never attained.
Brows lowered, unhurried, she played on and on,
telling out all the boundless things within.
A light gather, a slow twist, a sweep, a pluck back —
first the *Nishang*, then the *Liu Yao*.

The thick strings roared like sudden rain;
the thin strings whispered like private talk.
Roar and whisper crossed and intermingled —
great pearls and small pearls falling on a jade plate.
Warbling, an oriole's song gliding under flowers;
half-choked, a spring running beneath the ice.
The icy spring turned cold and slow; the strings congealed and broke —
congealed, impassable, the sound paused for a while.
Then a hidden sorrow, a dark grievance rose:
here silence was better far than any sound.
A silver jar bursting, water flying;
armored horsemen charging, blades and spears ringing.
The tune ended; she swept the pick across the center —
four strings at once, like tearing silk.
In boats east and west no one spoke a word;
only the autumn moon, white in the heart of the river.

Musing, she tucked the pick back through the strings,
straightened her clothes, and rose with a composed face.
She said she had been a girl of the capital,
and lived below the hill at Xiamaling.
At thirteen she had mastered the pipa,
her name listed in the Jiaofang's first division.
When she finished a tune, even master musicians yielded;
dressed and painted, she made Qiuniang herself jealous.
Young men of Wuling vied to press silk rewards on her —
one song, and red gauze past all counting.
Jeweled, silver-toothed combs snapped as she kept time;
her blood-red silk skirts fouled by spilled wine.
Joy this year, joy the next;
autumn moon and spring breeze were idly spent.
Then her brother left for the army, her aunt died;
dusk went and dawn came, and her beauty faded.
Fewer horses at her door, the place grown cold;
growing old, she married a merchant.
A merchant values profit and thinks lightly of parting;
last month he went to Fuliang to buy tea.
She keeps an empty boat alone at the river's mouth,
the moon bright around it, the river water cold.
Deep in the night she dreams of her young days,
and weeps within the dream, tears cutting red channels through her rouge.

I had already sighed on hearing the pipa;
hearing her words, I sighed again.
Both of us are people brought low at the ends of the earth —
now that we meet, why need we have known each other before?
Since last year I have taken leave of the imperial capital,
banished and ill in bed in the town of Xunyang.
Xunyang is remote, and here there is no music;
all year I never hear string or flute.
I live near the Pen River on low, damp ground,
yellow reeds and bitter bamboo growing around the house.
What do I hear there from dawn to dusk?
A cuckoo crying blood, a gibbon wailing.
Spring river and flower-filled mornings, autumn moonlit nights —
often I pour out wine and drink alone.
Are there no mountain songs and village flutes?
They squawk and grate — hard to sit and listen to.
Tonight I hear your pipa speak,
and it is like celestial music; my ears grow clear for a moment.
Do not decline — sit down and play one more tune,
and for you I compose a *Song of the Pipa*.

Moved by my words, she stood there a long while,
then sat and tightened the strings, and they quickened.
Mournful, unlike anything she played before,
the whole room, hearing it again, covered their faces and wept.
And whose tears fell the most of all there?
The Jiangzhou vice-prefect — his blue gown soaked through.

source.title: 如梦令·常记溪亭日暮
source.author: 李清照
source.text:
常记溪亭日暮，沉醉不知归路。
兴尽晚回舟，误入藕花深处。
争渡，争渡，惊起一滩鸥鹭。

translation:
I often recall the Stream Pavilion at dusk,
so deep in wine I knew no way home.
When joy was spent, I turned the boat back late
and strayed into the heart of the lotus.
Push through, push through —
startling up a whole sandbar of gulls and herons.

source.title: 浣溪沙·一曲新词酒一杯
source.author: 晏殊
source.text:
一曲新词酒一杯，去年天气旧亭台。夕阳西下几时回？
无可奈何花落去，似曾相识燕归来。小园香径独徘徊。

source.title: 山居秋暝
source.author: 王维
source.text:
空山新雨后，天气晚来秋。
明月松间照，清泉石上流。
竹喧归浣女，莲动下渔舟。
随意春芳歇，王孙自可留。

translation:
Empty hills after the fresh rain;
the evening turns to autumn.
The bright moon shines among the pines,
clear water slips over the stones.
Noise in the bamboo — the washerwomen return;
a stir in the lotus — the fishing boat drifts down.
Let spring's blossoms fade as they will —
the nobleman can well remain.

source.title: 卜算子·我住长江头
source.author: 李之仪
source.text:
我住长江头，君住长江尾。
日日思君不见君，共饮长江水。
此水几时休，此恨何时已。
只愿君心似我心，定不负相思意。

translation:
I live at the head of the Yangtze,
you live at its mouth.
Day after day I think of you and never see you—
yet together we drink the Yangtze's water.

When will this water cease to flow?
When will this sorrow ever end?
I only wish your heart were as my heart;
then surely neither of us will fail this longing.

source.title: 武陵春·春晚
source.author: 李清照
source.text:
风住尘香花已尽，日晚倦梳头。
物是人非事事休，欲语泪先流。
闻说双溪春尚好，也拟泛轻舟。
只恐双溪舴艋舟，载不动许多愁。

translation:
The wind has stilled; in fragrant dust the flowers are spent.
The day is late — too weary now to comb my hair.

Things remain, but people are gone; all things are done with.
I would speak, and first the tears flow.

I hear the spring at Twin Streams is still fair;
I too thought of drifting there in a light boat.
But I fear the skiff on Twin Streams
Could not carry so much sorrow.

source.title: 念奴娇·赤壁怀古
source.author: 苏轼
source.text:
大江东去，浪淘尽、千古风流人物。
故垒西边，人道是、三国周郎赤壁。
乱石穿空，惊涛拍岸，卷起千堆雪。
江山如画，一时多少豪杰。
遥想公瑾当年，小乔初嫁了，雄姿英发。
羽扇纶巾，谈笑处、樯橹灰飞烟灭。
故国神游，多情应笑我，早生华发。
人间如梦，一尊还酹江月。

translation:
The great river flows east;
its waves have washed away
the heroes of a thousand ages.
West of the old ramparts,
they say, stand the Red Cliffs
of young Zhou, lord of the Three Kingdoms.

Jagged rocks pierce the sky,
thundering breakers beat the shore,
rolling up a thousand heaps of snow.
River and hills — a painting:
how many heroes in that age!

I think back to Gongjin in his day,
just wed to Xiao Qiao,
his bearing heroic, radiant.
Feather fan, silk headband —
amid talk and laughter,
enemy masts and hulls
scattered to ash and smoke.

My spirit wanders that old realm;
should those of feeling laugh at me —
white hair has come too soon.
The world is but a dream;
I pour one cup
as a libation to the river moon.

source.title: 登高
source.author: 杜甫
source.text:
风急天高猿啸哀，渚清沙白鸟飞回。
无边落木萧萧下，不尽长江滚滚来。
万里悲秋常作客，百年多病独登台。
艰难苦恨繁霜鬓，潦倒新停浊酒杯。

source.title: 江城子·乙卯正月二十日夜记梦
source.author: 苏轼
source.text:
十年生死两茫茫，不思量，自难忘。
千里孤坟，无处话凄凉。
纵使相逢应不识，尘满面，鬓如霜。
夜来幽梦忽还乡，小轩窗，正梳妆。
相顾无言，惟有泪千行。
料得年年肠断处，明月夜，短松冈。

translation:
Jiangchengzi: Yimao Year, First Month, Twentieth Night — Recording a Dream

Ten years, the living and the dead — a mist between us both;
I do not force myself to think, yet never forget.
A lonely grave a thousand miles away,
nowhere to speak of this chill desolation.
Even were we to meet, you would not know me:
dust upon my face, my temples white as frost.

Last night in a dim dream I suddenly came home:
the small window, and you there, combing your hair.
We looked at each other without a word —
only tears, a thousand lines.
And I can guess where, year after year, the heart will break:
the moonlit night, the hill of short pines.

source.title: 永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古
source.author: 辛弃疾
source.text:
千古江山，英雄无觅，孙仲谋处。
舞榭歌台，风流总被、雨打风吹去。
斜阳草树，寻常巷陌，人道寄奴曾住。
想当年，金戈铁马，气吞万里如虎。
元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。
四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路。
可堪回首，佛狸祠下，一片神鸦社鼓。
凭谁问、廉颇老矣，尚能饭否？

translation:
A thousand ages pass; the rivers and hills remain—
nowhere to find a hero like Sun Zhongmou.
Dance terraces, song platforms—
their grace, all borne away by wind and rain.
Slanting sun, grass and trees,
the common lanes and streets—people say Jinu once lived here.
Think of those years: golden halberds, iron horses,
a breath that swallowed ten thousand li like a tiger.

In Yuanjia, the venture, rash and ill-prepared,
seeking to raise a victory mound at Langjuxu,
won only a panicked glance back north.
Forty-three years—still, as I gaze out,
I recall the beacon fires on the roads of Yangzhou.
How can I bear to look back: beneath the shrine of Bili,
a whole expanse of sacred crows, the beat of drums at the village rite.
Who is there to ask: old Lian Po,
can he still eat his fill?

source.title: 蝶恋花·伫倚危楼风细细
source.author: 柳永
source.text:
伫倚危楼风细细，望极春愁，黯黯生天际。
草色烟光残照里，无言谁会凭阑意。
拟把疏狂图一醉，对酒当歌，强乐还无味。
衣带渐宽终不悔，为伊消得人憔悴。

translation:
Standing long against the high tower in a gentle breeze,
I gaze to the farthest reach; spring sorrow
dimly rises at the sky's edge.

Grass color and misty light within the last glow—
wordless, who understands my leaning on the rail?

I mean to court wild abandon and drink myself drunk,
raise cup and song—yet forced joy still tastes of nothing.
My belt grows ever looser—yet I do not regret it in the end:
for her I waste away, haggard.
